artifacts.summary: Confirms both H4 gate matcher failures under the deployed grep, provides two empirically-verified corrected patterns (numbering-tolerant heading, boundary-free table check), and inventories every migration site needed to port the gate into the base orchestrate engine.

next_steps: Run /plan 128 to create an implementation plan for the matcher fix and the H4 gate migration into skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md.

memory_candidates.content: The deployed grep on this system is ugrep 7.8.4. Its POSIX/DFA -E engine mis-evaluates a \b word-boundary anchor when it occurs downstream of an earlier \b-anchored subexpression separated by a variable-width run like [^|]* -- every fragment matches alone but the composed pattern doesn't. Two fixes both work empirically: drop the \b entirely (safe when surrounding structural delimiters like | already do the discriminating), or add -P to force the PCRE2 engine which evaluates the composition correctly. Prefer dropping \b to avoid a new engine-flag dependency, unless boundary precision is load-bearing.

This repo's two orchestrate engine files (skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md and skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md) use an explicit 'Asymmetry decision (recorded, not acted on)' comment convention when a fix or feature is deliberately applied to only one of the two files instead of mirrored to both. Reuse this convention (grep for the phrase in skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md for a worked example) whenever a co-maintenance contract's escape clause is invoked instead of dual-editing.
